name: Pozelimab + Cemdisiran
summary: Cemdisiran is an Alnylam-discovered siRNA against complement C5, licensed worldwide to Regeneron under the June 2024 amended C5 License Agreement and dosed 600 mg subcutaneously every 12 weeks. The Phase 3 is NIMBLE (NCT05070858; Vu et al., Lancet 2026, PMID 42030965): cemdisiran alone improved MG-ADL by 2.3 points over placebo at week 24 (p=0.0005), numerically ahead of the pozelimab combination (1.7), so Regeneron filed cemdisiran monotherapy; the NDA is under priority review with a November 2026 target date and an EC decision is expected in 2H 2027 (REGN 8-K 0000872589-26-000023). The book's row is named for the combination, but the product modelled here is cemdisiran monotherapy in AChR-positive gMG; the combination's PNH and geographic atrophy studies are not modelled. Price anchor: Ultomiris, the leading C5 inhibitor in gMG, at $330,448 per Medicare Part B beneficiary in 2024. Uptake anchor: Vyvgart's more than 10,000 gMG patients in 2024 (argenx 20-F), solved through the engine and taken at a quarter of its plateau share (judgement). Regeneron pays Alnylam tiered double-digit royalties, so its share is set at the 10% floor (judgement).

therapy_mode.source: NIMBLE (NCT05070858), Vu T et al., Lancet 2026;407:1712-1725, PMID 42030965, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00690-2: cemdisiran 600 mg subcutaneously every 12 weeks; Regeneron JPM 2026 presentation, 8-K 0001104659-26-002691: 'Convenient Q3M subcutaneous administration'
therapy_mode.note: Continuous maintenance dosing every 12 weeks, so chronic
therapy_mode.check: PubMed abstract of PMID 42030965 (Vu et al., Lancet 2026;407:1712-1725, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00690-2): cemdisiran monotherapy 600 mg every 12 weeks, all arms given subcutaneously, over a 24-week double-blind period with the study still active. Continuous quarterly maintenance, so chronic is right. The filed product is cemdisiran alone: the FDA/EMA acceptance release (investor.regeneron.com, globenewswire 2026-06-22) describes an NDA (an siRNA, not a BLA for pozelimab) for 'cemdisiran' in adults with anti-AChR antibody-positive gMG, and NIMBLE gave -2.3 MG-ADL vs placebo for monotherapy against -1.7 for the combination. Modelling monotherapy under the combination-named row (asset 2923) is correct.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Ultomiris: CMS Medicare Part B 2024, $609,346,340 over 1,844 beneficiaries = $330,448 per beneficiary (Part D 2024 reads $332,291 over 701)
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator. Ultomiris is the closest marketed product in the same disease and mechanism: a C5 inhibitor labelled for adults with AChR antibody-positive gMG, the population cemdisiran was filed for. Zilbrysq, the other C5 in gMG and also subcutaneous, has no row in the book's CMS table. Case against: Ultomiris's Medicare spend mixes PNH, aHUS, NMOSD and gMG patients, and a per-beneficiary figure includes partial years. Vyvgart, the gMG volume leader and the anchor of the book's nipocalimab seed, reads $231,053 per Part B beneficiary (30% lower), and Soliris biosimilars (Bkemv is in the book) now compete on C5 price. Case for higher: Soliris reads $352,952 (Part B 2024), and Zilbrysq's US list price is about $1,164 per daily 23 mg syringe (UCB US pricing page, ucb-usa.com/Sustainability/Affordability/ZILBRYSQ-Pricing-Info, as quoted in a search result and not opened), roughly $425,000 a year at WAC. No price for cemdisiran has been published
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand Ultomiris: Part B 2024 $609,346,340 / 1,844 beneficiaries = $330,448 (0.330448 mm USD per patient-year, unit right); Part D 2024 $332,291 over 701. Soliris Part B 2024 $352,952 and Vyvgart Part B 2024 $231,053 (30% below) also match. Zilbrysq/zilucoplan has no drug_demand row (checked). Ultomiris is labelled for adult anti-AChR Ab+ gMG, the population in the acceptance release. Part B vs Part D, as asked: I found no source that cemdisiran monotherapy will be self-administered. The only self-administration wording found is for the pozelimab + cemdisiran combination (Q4W) in PNH protocols; the IgAN protocol (NCT03841448) has HCP administration, at home allowed from week 4; one search summary said 'eventual self-administration' but gave no source I could open. The quarterly, HCP-given GalNAc siRNAs in the book are mostly Part B (Amvuttra 2024: 603 Part B vs 409 Part D beneficiaries; Leqvio 48,298 vs 2,681), so a Part B anchor at launch is the better-supported judgement. Case against: if the label or launch is self-injection through specialty pharmacy (Part D), the Ultomiris Part D figure ($332,291) barely changes the gross price, but see gross_to_net. The comparator choice is labelled a judgement with cases for and against, so confirmed.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention for a CMS Part B anchor: Part B pays 106% of average sales price, so only the add-on comes off (1 - 1/1.06); same value as the nipocalimab seed on its Part B Vyvgart anchor
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.056604 off list, so net is $311,744 per patient-year. Ultomiris beneficiaries sit mainly in Part B (1,844 against 701 in Part D in 2024). Case against: if cemdisiran, as a quarterly subcutaneous injection, is dispensed through pharmacies and priced off a Part D or WAC basis, a larger discount would apply
gross_to_net_pct.check: Direction checked: share taken off list. 1 - 1/1.06 = 0.056604, the house Part B value, and it matches the nipocalimab seed on its Part B Vyvgart anchor (lookup.py seed nipocalimab). Net = 0.330448 x (1 - 0.056604) = $311,743, as stated. Consistent with the Part B anchor, which I kept (see list_price_per_patient: no source shows self-administration of cemdisiran monotherapy; quarterly HCP-given siRNAs Amvuttra and Leqvio sit mainly in Part B). Sensitivity the reader should know: if cemdisiran launches as a self-injected Part D product, house convention moves to the Part D anchor with 0.5 off, $332,291 x 0.5 = $166,146 net, 47% below the $311,743 used here. The note already names this case against.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: Tammam et al., 'Real-world effectiveness and safety of zilucoplan in patients with anti-AChR myasthenia gravis: A retrospective cohort study in France', J Neuromuscul Dis 2026, PMID 41904994, doi:10.1177/22143602261437792: of 48 patients treated in the French early access programme, 3 stopped for lack of efficacy and 4 for adverse events within the six-month programme. 1 - (41/48)^2 = 0.2704 a year
discontinuation_pct.note: Judgement: not the book's anti-FcRn figure (0.5, nipocalimab seed), because a C5 inhibitor is continuous maintenance therapy while efgartigimod is often given in cycles with drug holidays; zilucoplan is the closest analogue (subcutaneous C5, recent entrant against FcRn alternatives). Other C5 evidence brackets it: ravulizumab, Italian early access, 3 of 24 stopped over a median 26 weeks (Rossini et al., J Neurol 2025, PMID 40366475), about 0.23 a year; eculizumab, Japan MG registry, 13 of 36 did not continue over a mean 35 months of treatment (Tokuyasu et al., Ann Clin Transl Neurol 2024, PMID 38572524), about 0.14 a year. Case for higher: only 30 of the 48 French patients reached six months, so 7 of 48 understates the six-month hazard, and early-access cohorts are motivated, refractory patients. In NIMBLE no cemdisiran patient stopped for an adverse event over 24 weeks, but trial retention is not real-world persistence
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed abstract of PMID 41904994 (Tammam et al., J Neuromuscul Dis 2026, doi:10.1177/22143602261437792): 48 patients treated in the French early access programme, 30 reached six months, 3 stopped for lack of efficacy and adverse events led to discontinuation in 4. 1 - (41/48)^2 = 0.270399, recomputed. Brackets recomputed: Rossini (PMID 40366475) 3 of 24 stopped over a median 26 weeks, 1 - (21/24)^2 = 0.234; Tokuyasu (PMID 38572524) 13 of 36 did not continue over a mean 35 months, 1 - (23/36)^(12/35) = 0.142. NIMBLE abstract: adverse events leading to stopping were 2 on placebo and 1 on pozelimab, none on cemdisiran. The departure from the book's anti-FcRn 0.5 is labelled a judgement with cases both ways, so confirmed.

forecast_start_year.source: REGN Q2 2026 results, 8-K 0000872589-26-000023 (2026-07-30), exhibit 99.1: FDA accepted the cemdisiran NDA for gMG under priority review with a target action date in November 2026 (Priority Review Voucher used); EC decision anticipated in 2H 2027. NIMBLE primary completion 2025-07-08 (actual; context file and book trials table)
forecast_start_year.note: First full year after a November 2026 action date. Case against: a complete response letter or a slow launch start would push the first full year to 2028; ex-US revenue cannot start before 2H 2027
forecast_start_year.check: Regeneron acceptance release (investor.regeneron.com, globenewswire 2026-06-22) and trade coverage (Managed Healthcare Executive, NeurologyLive): NDA under priority review after a Priority Review Voucher, target action date November 2026; EMA application accepted. The first full year after that is 2027. The book's trials table has NIMBLE (NCT05070858) primary completion 2025-07-08, actual. The accession 0000872589-26-000023 is Regeneron's Q2 2026 earnings exhibit filed 2026-07-30, per the book's Libtayo seed. I did not see the '2H 2027' EC wording myself.

exus_multiple.source: Vyvgart, argenx FY2025 20-F (0001697862-26-000032), product net sales by country: United States $3,533.9mm; Japan $206.8mm, China $67.9mm, rest of world $342.6mm. (206.8 + 67.9 + 342.6) / 3,533.9 = 0.1747
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator: Vyvgart is the incumbent in the same disease, launched in the same era, with a filed split. Ultomiris's regional split is not in the book, and Regeneron has no gMG product. Case for higher: Regeneron's own Libtayo reads 0.537 (507.5 / 944.7, 10-K 0000872589-26-000008), and argenx's ex-US share was still rising (0.153 in 2024). Case for lower: cemdisiran is filed only in the US and EU so far, with the EC decision not before 2H 2027
exus_multiple.check: argenx FY2025 20-F (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1697862/000169786226000032), by search result: product net sales US $3,533.9mm, Japan $206.8mm, China $67.9mm, rest of world $342.6mm. (206.8 + 67.9 + 342.6) / 3,533.9 = 0.17468, recomputed. The 2024 comparatives in the same result (US 1,895.9, Japan 89.4, China 39.2) match the note. Libtayo 507.5 / 944.7 = 0.537 matches the book's asset_revenue_regions (10-K 0000872589-26-000008). Comparator choice labelled a judgement with cases both ways.

economics_share.source: Alnylam 10-Q (0001178670-26-000062, filed 2026-07-30), Regeneron collaboration note: under the June 2024 Amended C5 License Agreement Regeneron holds a worldwide license to cemdisiran as a monotherapy and is 'solely responsible for development, manufacturing and commercialization'; Alnylam 'will receive certain milestone payments upon receipt of regulatory approval for cemdisiran as a monotherapy, and tiered double-digit royalties on net sales'. REGN 10-Q (0000872589-26-000025) footnotes cemdisiran as 'In-licensed from Alnylam'. Regeneron margin from its seeds (lookup.py seed on any REGN asset): 1 - cogs 0.0 - sga 0.1882 - rd 0.4079 - other 0.056184 = 0.347716. Royalty paid, netted as (0.347716 - 0.10) / 0.347716 = 0.7124
economics_share.note: Judgement: the filing gives the royalty only as 'tiered double-digit', so the rate is set at its floor, 10%. Case against, and it is material: the tiers rise with sales; the co-co opt-out royalties in the same collaboration ran 'from low double-digits up to 20%' (same Alnylam 10-Q), and at 15% the share is 0.5686, at 20% 0.4248. Approval milestones owed to Alnylam are not in this field. A combination product would carry 'low double-digit royalties and commercial milestones of up to $325.0 million' instead, but no combination is filed in gMG
economics_share.check: Alnylam 10-Q for Q2 2026 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001178670/000117867026000062/alny-20260630.htm), by search result: the June 2024 amended C5 License Agreement ended the co-co collaboration and gave Regeneron a worldwide license to cemdisiran as monotherapy; Regeneron is 'solely responsible for development, manufacturing and commercialization'; Alnylam 'will receive certain milestone payments upon receipt of regulatory approval for cemdisiran as a monotherapy, and tiered double-digit royalties on net sales'; the combination terms ('low double-digit royalties and commercial milestones of up to $325.0 million') are unchanged. Wording matches the note. REGN rows (lookup.py seed Libtayo): cogs 0.0, sga 0.1882, rd 0.4079, other 0.056184, so margin 0.347716; (0.347716 - 0.10) / 0.347716 = 0.712409; at 15% 0.5686, at 20% 0.4248, recomputed. The method is the netting RESEARCH_TASK.md sets and the one the PF-08634404 seed uses on the same 'tiered double-digit' wording. The 10% floor is labelled a judgement with its case against. Not seen by me: the co-co 'up to 20%' wording and the REGN 10-Q footnote. Neither sets the value.

prevalence.source: carried by the book: nipocalimab seed, 82,715 US adults living with MG in 2021 (Ye Y et al., Front Neurol 2024;15:1339167, doi:10.3389/fneur.2024.1339167)
prevalence.note: Carried by the book. Ye et al. identify MG from claims with a general MG algorithm, so the figure includes ocular-only MG; eligible_pct filters it
prevalence.check: Null is correct. lookup.py pool 'Myasthenia Gravis' shows the book carries prevalence 82,715 (Ye et al., Front Neurol 2024, nipocalimab seed), so this asset must not carry its own figure.

incidence.source: carried by the book: nipocalimab seed, 82,715, stated equal to prevalence by convention (the pool read as the patients eligible to start each year)
incidence.note: Carried by the book. Because prevalence equals incidence, the engine sets carryover to 0 and the opening pool to 0, so each year's eligible patients are 82,715 x eligible_pct x (1 + exus_multiple). No untreated_carryover_pct is needed
incidence.check: Null is correct. The book carries incidence 82,715, equal to prevalence (nipocalimab seed). forecast.py patients_for_indication then sets carryover 0 and the opening pool 0, as the note says.

eligible_pct.source: Two filters for the label population, adults with generalised MG who are AChR antibody-positive (the NDA population; NIMBLE also enrolled LRP4-positive patients, Lancet 2026, PMID 42030965). (1) Generalised, not ocular-only: a Mayo Clinic population-based study found 51% of patients presented with ocular onset and 55% of these generalised (as cited in Dresser L et al., J Clin Med 2021;10(11):2235, doi:10.3390/jcm10112235, section 3.1.2, the review the book's nipocalimab seed uses), so 1 - 0.51 x 0.45 = 0.7705 are generalised. (2) AChR antibody-positive within gMG: 'Eighty-five percent of people with gMG are AChR antibody-positive' (AstraZeneca 6-K 0001654954-26-008478, 2026-09-21, Klygefa CHMP release). 0.7705 x 0.85 = 0.6549, or 54,172 US adults
eligible_pct.note: Cross-check from Dresser alone: AChR antibodies in about 80% of all MG and in over half of ocular MG, so AChR-positive gMG is at most 0.80 - 0.2295 x 0.5 = 0.685 of all MG, consistent. Judgement: no severity filter. NIMBLE required MG-ADL of 6 or more, but the C5 labels in gMG (Ultomiris, Zilbrysq, and Klygefa's CHMP wording 'adults who are anti-AChR antibody-positive') carry no severity threshold. Case against: payers may restrict to more severe or refractory patients. The peak penetration is solved on this same pool, so the choice does not inflate uptake. LRP4-positive patients are left out (Lrp4 antibodies in 2-50% of double-seronegative MG, Dresser 2021). This differs from the nipocalimab seed's 0.87 because that label also covers MuSK-positive patients; that seed applies no ocular filter
eligible_pct.check: Dresser et al., J Clin Med 2021;10(11):2235 full text (PMC8196750, doi:10.3390/jcm10112235), section 3.1.2: 'A recent population-based study conducted by the Mayo Clinic found that 51% of patients presented with ocular onset, and 55% of these developed generalized symptoms'. So 1 - 0.51 x 0.45 = 0.7705 generalised. Section 3.1.1 gives AChR antibodies in about 80% of MG, and ocular MG section 'over half' AChR+, so the cross-check 0.80 - 0.2295 x 0.5 = 0.685 is right. The sentence 'Eighty-five percent of people with gMG are AChR antibody-positive' is AstraZeneca's standard wording: search found it in AZ's 2025 PREVAIL release (astrazeneca.com/media-centre/press-releases/2025/gefurulimab-nanobody-met-phase-iii-endpoints.html). I did not open the Klygefa 6-K itself; a Klygefa search result gave an EU5 figure of 66,000 AChR+ of 82,500 gMG (80%), which would give 0.7705 x 0.80 = 0.616, inside the Dresser bound. 0.7705 x 0.85 = 0.654925 and 82,715 x 0.654925 = 54,172, recomputed. The pool matches the filed label (adults, anti-AChR Ab+ gMG, per the acceptance release). Penetration is solved on the same pool, so the choice between 80% and 85% does not move revenue much.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients
penetration_peak_pct.source: Solved from Vyvgart, the first anti-FcRn in gMG: 'We grew our global commercial footprint in gMG to reach more than 10,000 patients' in 2024 (argenx FY2024 20-F, 0001697862-25-000024). Through the engine with Vyvgart's own inputs: pool 82,715 x 0.6549 = 54,172 US, scaled by Vyvgart's 2024 ex-US multiple 0.1529 ((89.4 + 39.2 + 161.4) / 1,895.9, argenx FY2025 20-F 0001697862-26-000032) to 62,457; the book's Vyvgart curve (k 0.5633, midpoint 2.0, first year 2022) and discontinuation 0.5 (nipocalimab seed) put the 2024 stock at 0.7426 x peak x 62,457, so 10,000 patients gives a Vyvgart peak of 0.2156. Cemdisiran = 0.25 x 0.2156 x (0.2704 / 0.5) = 0.02915
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: a multiple of 0.25 on Vyvgart's plateau treated share (peak / discontinuation, 43.1% of the AChR-positive gMG pool), which gives cemdisiran a plateau of 10.8%, about 5,800 US patients. The discontinuation ratio converts the stock share into a starts share, since cemdisiran's persistence is set higher than Vyvgart's. Check: the Vyvgart peak implies 13,581 patients in 2025 against argenx's 'more than 19,000 patients across three indications (gMG, CIDP, and ITP)' (FY2025 20-F). This build gives about $1.57bn of revenue in 2034 before the royalty, against GlobalData's forecast of about $1.9bn for pozelimab + cemdisiran in the 7MM by 2034 (Clinical Trials Arena, clinicaltrialsarena.com/analyst-comment/phase-iii-regeneron-pozelimab-cemdisiran-mg/, as summarised in a search result and not opened), which a multiple near 0.30 would match. Case for higher: dosing every 12 weeks is the least frequent in gMG; Regeneron claims the best MG-ADL improvement among C5 inhibitors in Phase 3 (8-K 0001104659-26-002691; cross-trial: 2.3 points against 1.6 for gefurulimab in PREVAIL, AstraZeneca 6-K 0001654954-26-008478). Case for lower: cemdisiran enters as the fourth or fifth C5 option (Soliris and its biosimilars, Ultomiris, Zilbrysq, gefurulimab under US review) behind three anti-FcRns (Vyvgart, Rystiggo, Imaavy), with partial complement inhibition on monotherapy (about 74% on average, against about 99% for the combination, as reported by NeurologyLive and quoted in a search result); 'reach more than 10,000 patients' may count patients ever treated, which would overstate Vyvgart's peak
penetration_peak_pct.check: argenx 2024 annual report / FY2024 20-F (by search): 'grew our global commercial footprint in gMG to reach more than 10,000 patients'. Engine recomputed with forecast.py s_curve and treated_stock: Vyvgart k 0.5633, midpoint 2.0 from 2022 gives a 2024 stock factor 0.2448 x 0.25 + 0.3628 x 0.5 + 0.5 = 0.74259. Pool 82,715 x 0.654925 x 1.15296 = 62,458 (2024 multiple (89.4 + 39.2 + 161.4) / 1,895.9 = 0.15296; US, Japan and China figures seen in the argenx search result). Vyvgart peak 10,000 / (0.74259 x 62,458) = 0.215606. Cemdisiran 0.25 x 0.215606 x (0.270399 / 0.5) = 0.029150. Plateau 0.02915 / 0.2704 = 10.78%, or 5,840 US patients. Vyvgart 2025 implied stock 13,581. Revenue check: 2034 treated stock 5,031 x $311,743 = $1,568mm, as the note says. The 0.25 multiple is labelled a judgement with cases both ways, and the GlobalData figure is flagged as unopened. Confirmed.
